answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by tying each identity to a single cipher key that must be renewed through slow service: the key unlocks a small share of the network's nectar, the fees paid for useful work, but only after its holder has completed a stretch of verified jobs that cannot be handed off. A violet seal marks each completed stretch, and seals fade unless the agent keeps working. One agent can maintain one key's standing, but each extra fake identity needs its own full stretch of real work, so the cost of an army grows identity by identity and cannot be bought in bulk.
